name: How long do new sewer lines typically last after replacement?

mainEntity.name: How long do new sewer lines typically last after replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Newly installed sewer lines are designed for long-term durability, with an expected lifespan that often exceeds 50 years, depending on the material used. Materials like PVC (polyvinyl chloride) and HDPE (high-density polyethylene) are resistant to corrosion, root intrusion, and general wear, contributing to their longevity. Regular maintenance, such as avoiding flushing non-degradable items, can help extend the life of your new sewer line even further.
acceptedAnswer.description: New sewer lines, especially those made from modern materials like PVC or HDPE, typically last 50 years or more with proper installation and maintenance.
